raw_response:
Seventy-four years old this year. Fifty years I've been working these 3 mu. My wife and I are the only ones left at home — the kids went to the city long ago, they send a little money and come back for the big holidays. The land is all I know.

Three mu isn't much, but it feeds us and gives a little grain to sell. I do wheat and maize, same as most everyone in the village. That's how it's been for many years now. When I was younger we did cotton too, but cotton takes too much work for old bones, and the price isn't what it used to be. Wheat and maize — the machines come and do most of it, you just pay them by the mu.

**Wheat first.** I plant in early October, usually around the 8th or 10th, depending on when the maize comes off. I use improved seed from the agricultural supply shop — the 'Jimai' variety has done well for me these last few years. I save a little seed from a good plot each year too, but mostly I buy. About 15 kg of seed per mu, a bit thick because at my age I'd rather have too many plants than not enough.

For fertilizer, I put down one bag of compound fertilizer (15-15-15) before planting — that's about 40 kg per mu as base. Then at green-up in March, I topdress with urea, maybe 15 kg per mu. The extension fellow who came through the village a few years back said that's about right for our yield target. My neighbor Old Wang uses a little more but his land is in the low spot, holds more water. Mine's fine with what I give it.

Irrigation — I'll water three times if the winter is dry. Once before winter to settle the soil, once at jointing in late March/early April (that's the most important one), and once at grain-filling in May. The well is shared with two other households; the electricity is metered now, so you don't waste water like we used to.

Pesticide — I'll spray herbicide once in spring for the broadleaf weeds. If I see aphids at heading, I spray once. That's it. Too much spraying costs money.

**Then maize right after.** The combine harvests wheat around June 8-10, and I have to get maize in within a week. I hire the no-till seeder that comes through the village — 30 yuan per mu, they plant right through the wheat stubble. Hybrid seed, something like Zhengdan 958 or whatever the shop recommends that year — about 45 yuan per mu.

At planting, I put 25 kg of compound fertilizer per mu down with the seeder. Then at big trumpet stage (around end of July), I topdress urea, maybe 20 kg per mu. Maize is hungrier than wheat. If it's been dry, I irrigate once at tasseling — that's the critical time. Usually the summer rain is enough, but not always.

My yield hopes: wheat maybe 450 kg/mu if the weather holds, maize 500 kg/mu. Some years better, some worse. Last year wheat was only 400 because of the late frost, but maize was good.

Labor — it's just us. My wife helps with weeding and watching the field. The heavy work I hire out: tillage, planting, harvesting, all by the mu. For 3 mu, my own hands and back do maybe 20 days of work across the whole year. The rest is machines and some hired help at harvest if my sons can't come back.

Money is tight but manageable at this scale. The seed and fertilizer are the big costs, then the custom machinery. I don't take on debt for inputs — at my age, that's not wise.
